claims: 5G is the fifth-generation global cellular network standard.
5G utilizes a mix of low-, mid-, and high-band (millimeter wave) frequencies.
Key components of 5G include the 5G Core and New Radio (NR) RAN.
5G low latency is around 30 ms or less.
5G supports up to 1 million devices per square kilometer.
Network Slicing enables operators to create isolated virtual networks tailored to specific use cases with unique quality-of-service (QoS) requirements.
FR1 frequency range is sub-7.125 GHz.
FR1 uses low- and mid-band frequencies.
Massive MIMO utilizes large numbers of antennas on base stations to send and receive more signals simultaneously.
Small Cells are miniature transmitters crucial for expanding mmWave coverage in cities.
5G Core (5GC) is a cloud-native core network.
5G Core (5GC) is more flexible and software-defined than previous generations.
Initial 5G deployments (Non-Standalone) relied on existing 4G infrastructure.
Standalone 5G networks offer full 5G performance without 4G anchors.
5G-Advanced is evolving toward the end of 2026 to incorporate enhanced AI/ML and extended reality (XR) capabilities.
